mainTopic: רבי יהודה's reason for מנחת סולת, רב פפא's question about 'מיני מנחה,' and who taught 'bring all five'
overview: Before this amud, the גמרא suggested that for רבי יהודה, someone who vows a plain מנחה brings מנחת סולת because the פסוק lists it first. The גמרא challenges this from a משנה: a plain עולה vow needs only a lamb, not the bull that comes first in the פסוק, and רבי יהודה does not argue. So the גמרא gives a new reason: מנחת סולת is the one called just 'מנחה,' with no added name. The 'opens first' wording is only a memory sign. Next, רב פפא asks whether a vow of 'מיני מנחה,' which mixes plural and singular, means one מנחה or two. Proofs from the משנה and from a ברייתא are each pushed aside, the second because the ברייתא may follow רבי שמעון, who allows one מנחה of half loaves and half wafers. Finally the גמרא asks who taught that someone who forgot which מנחה he specified brings all five. רבי ירמיה says it cannot be רבי שמעון, because his view would create fourteen possibilities. אביי answers that it can be רבי שמעון, since he allows bringing an offering with a condition. אביי begins to prove this from a ברייתא about a doubtful מצורע, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If so, the first-mentioned animal should always be required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא extends the 'first in the פסוק' reasoning to every kind of עולה: cattle means a bull, flock means a lamb, birds means תורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...first. Likewise, if he said 'from the flock,' he should bring a lamb, since the פסוק mentions it first. If he said 'from birds,' he should bring תורים, since the פסוק mentions them first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list of what would follow if רבי יהודה's 'first in the פסוק' reasoning were applied to עולות. This is setting up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the item the תורה lists first is the default, then each section of the עולה passage in ויקרא א should have a default too. For cattle that is a bull, for the flock a lamb, and for birds תורים. The גמרא lays out these results so it can compare them with a משנה that seems to say otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because
The פסוק opened with it first, meaning it is the first item listed
Flock animals (sheep and goats)
A lamb
Turtledoves, the first bird listed for an עולה

phrases.english: first.
phrases.notes: This ends the line just before it: 'from cattle, he should bring a bull, since the פסוק opens with it first.'

phrases.english: 'From the flock': he should bring a lamb,
since the verse opens with it first.
'From the birds': he should bring doves,
since the verse opens with it first.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup for קשיא (extension of a premise)
steps.triggerLanguage: מן הצאן יביא כבש הואיל ופתח בו הכתוב תחלה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the 'if so' extension of רבי יהודה's reasoning, which began just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's principle that an unspecified vow defaults to the item the פסוק lists first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spells out what the principle would require for every kind of עולה, so these results can be tested against a משנה

steps.title: The משנה says a plain עולה vow is fulfilled with a lamb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the extension from a משנה: 'הרי עלי עולה' means a lamb, not a bull, and רבי יהודה does not argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why did we learn in a משנה: 'If someone says, "I take upon myself an עולה," he brings a lamb. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: a תור or a בן יונה.' And רבי יהודה does not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה that clashes with the 'first in the פסוק' rule. In that משנה, a plain עולה vow requires a lamb, and רבי יהודה stays silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'first in the פסוק' decided the matter, a plain עולה vow should require a bull, because cattle come first in the עולה passage. Instead, the תנא קמא requires only a lamb, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows even a bird. רבי יהודה does not object, which suggests he agrees and does not use the 'first in the פסוק' rule here.

keyTerms.meaning: But why...? This introduces a contradiction.
'I take upon myself an עולה,' a vow without saying which animal
A turtledove or a young pigeon, the two kinds of bird for an עולה
And he does not argue

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי יהודה's silence as nothing. In the גמרא, when a sage who argues elsewhere stays quiet, that silence counts as agreement, and that is exactly what makes this a challenge.

phrases.english: Why, then, did we learn in a mishna:
'It is upon me to bring a burnt offering': he must bring a lamb.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
a dove or a pigeon,
and Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלמה תנן הרי עלי עולה יביא כבש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the results laid out in step 1 against a משנה and finds a contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה's reason is 'the פסוק opens with it first'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By that reasoning, a plain עולה vow should require a bull. The משנה requires only a lamb, and רבי יהודה does not argue, so he does not seem to hold the 'first in the פסוק' rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: It forces the גמרא to find a different reason for רבי יהודה's ruling that a plain מנחה vow means מנחת סולת.

steps.title: A new meaning for 'the most notable meal offering': it has no added name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that מנחת סולת is 'the most notable' because it is called just 'מנחה,' with no extra description.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'the most notable of the meal offerings' mean? That it has no added name.
steps.whatsHappening: The 'first in the פסוק' reason ran into trouble, so the גמרא gives a different reason why רבי יהודה picks the מנחת סולת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other meal offerings in the פסוק each have a description attached, such as 'baked in an oven' or 'on a griddle.' The fine-flour one is called just 'מנחה.' So someone who vows a plain 'מנחה' means the one that is called only by that name. This reason does not depend on order, so the problem from עולה no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The most notable (special) of the meal offerings
An added name; a description attached to the basic name
A meal offering of plain fine flour

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is still saying 'it comes first in the פסוק.' The reason has changed completely: now it is about the name having no description.

phrases.english: Rather, what is 'the most notable of the meal offerings'?
phrases.notes: These are רבי יהודה's words about the מנחת סולת.

phrases.english: That it has no added name.
phrases.notes: The others are called things like 'baked in an oven' or 'on a griddle.' This one is just 'מנחה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the 'first in the פסוק' reasoning that was challenged in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the reason behind רבי יהודה's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מנחת סולת is chosen because it comes first in the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת סולת is chosen because it is the only one with no added name.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה himself gives the 'opens first' reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the תנא explicitly says the reason is that the verse opens with it first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא says 'since the verse opens with it first'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reason, because רבי יהודה's own words seem to give the old reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer says the reason is 'no added name.' But the text of the teaching says 'since the verse opens with it first.' That looks like the 'first in the פסוק' reason after all.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so...? This introduces a challenge from a source.
He says

phrases.english: But the תנא

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּפָתַח בּוֹ הַכָּתוּב תְּחִלָּה קָאָמַר?
phrases.english: says 'since the verse opens with it first'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תָּנָא הוֹאִיל וּפָתַח בּוֹ הַכָּתוּב תְּחִלָּה קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 3's new reason using the wording of the teaching itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 3 that the reason is 'no added name.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching explicitly says the reason is that the verse opens with it, which contradicts the new explanation.

steps.title: Reading the teaching as one connected sentence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the words: 'which is the notable one with no added name? The one the verse opens with.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Which meal offering is the most notable of the meal offerings, the one with no added name? It is the one the verse opens with first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the 'opens first' words as a way of pointing out which offering is meant, not as the reason for the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is still 'no added name.' The phrase 'the verse opens with it first' only identifies which offering that is. So the wording fits the new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the גמרא rereads the words)
Which one is it?

phrases.english: This is what he means:
Which meal offering is the most notable of the meal offerings,
the one that has no added name?
It is this one, the one the verse opens with first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by rereading the wording of the teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Since the verse opens with it first' is the reason for the ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those words only identify which offering has no added name.

steps.title: Why point it out? He already named the fine-flour offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this pointing-out is unnecessary, since רבי יהודה already said 'מנחת סולת' explicitly.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! He already says 'the fine-flour meal offering'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 5: if those words only identify the offering, they seem unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already named the מנחת סולת outright. So adding 'the one the verse opens with' tells us nothing new. Why would the teaching say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (an objection that something says nothing new)

phrases.english: That is obvious!
He says 'the fine-flour meal offering'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 5's reading as making the words unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 5's claim that 'opens first' just identifies the offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The offering was already named explicitly, so identifying it again adds nothing.

steps.title: It is just a memory sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'opens first' words are only a memory sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just a memory sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra words are there only to help us remember which offering רבי יהודה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are not a reason and do not carry new law. They are a memory aid: the one with no added name is the one at the start of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely a memory sign

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's real reason is that the מנחת סולת has no added name. 'The verse opens with it first' is only a memory sign, so the problem from עולה goes away.

phrases.english: It is just a memory sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 and closes the discussion of רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The words are a memory aid, not a source of law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words should teach something new.
steps.terutzMaskana: They only help us remember which offering is meant.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about the vow 'types of a meal offering'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about vowing 'מנחה' or 'מין המנחה,' and רב פפא asks about the mixed wording 'מיני מנחה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'A meal offering,' 'a type of meal offering,' and so on. רב פפא asks: if someone says 'types of a meal offering,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה, and רב פפא raises a question about a vow phrased half singular and half plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that singular wording ('a meal offering,' 'a type of meal offering') means one offering, and plural wording means two. 'מיני מנחה' has a plural word ('types') together with a singular word ('meal offering'). So it is unclear whether he must bring one offering or two.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of meal offering (singular wording)
Types of a meal offering (mixed singular and plural)
He asks (raises an open question)
What is the law?

phrases.english: 'A meal offering,' 'a type of meal offering,' etc.
רב פפא asks:
If he says 'types of a meal offering,' what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יהודה discussion and opens a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a vow worded 'מיני מנחה,' half plural and half singular, requires one meal offering or two.

steps.title: First side: 'types' means two meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains one side of רב פפא's question. Maybe the plural 'מיני' shows he means two מנחות, and the singular 'מנחה' is just the general name for all meal offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he said 'types' (plural), maybe he means two. Then why did he say 'meal offering' (singular)? Because all meal offerings together are also called 'meal offering,' as the פסוק says, 'And this is the law of the meal offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the first way to read the mixed wording 'מיני מנחה': the plural word decides, so he owes two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words point in two directions: 'מיני' is plural and 'מנחה' is singular. This side lets the plural win. It explains away the singular word by showing that the תורה itself uses 'מנחה' as a name for the whole group of meal offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Types / kinds (plural)
Two
They are called
The law of the meal offering. The singular word here covers all מנחות.

phrases.english: Since he said "types,"
he is saying two,
and what is the point of "meal offering" (singular)?
(all) meal offerings are also called "meal offering,"
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And this is the law of the meal offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of רב פפא's question from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the plural 'מיני' make it two מנחות, with the singular 'מנחה' read as a name for the whole category?

steps.title: Second side: 'meal offering' means only one
steps.stepSummary: The other side: maybe the singular 'מנחה' decides, so he owes one, and 'מיני מנחה' means 'one out of the types of meal offering.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps, since he said 'meal offering' (singular), he means one. Then why did he say 'types'? He meant: 'Out of the types of meal offering, I take upon myself one meal offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite reading: the singular word decides, so he owes only one מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the singular wins. The plural 'מיני' is explained as describing the choice he has ('one of the kinds'), not the number he must bring. This completes רב פפא's question with two equally possible readings.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. It introduces the second side of a question.
One

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
since he said "meal offering,"
he is saying one meal offering,
and what is the point of "types of a meal offering"?
This is what he is saying:
"Of the types of meal offering, one meal offering is upon me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר ״מִנְחָה״, חֲדָא מִנְחָה קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side to step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the singular 'מנחה' make it one מנחה, with 'מיני' meaning 'out of the kinds'?

steps.title: Attempted proof from the first clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove the 'two' side. The משנה says 'מנחה' or 'מין מנחה' requires one, which implies that 'מיני מנחה' requires two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'A meal offering' or 'a type of meal offering' means he brings one. So 'types of a meal offering' would mean two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from what the משנה implies: since the משנה lists only singular wordings as 'one,' a wording with a plural word should be two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits the 'bring one' rule to wordings that are fully singular. The גמרא reads that limit as excluding 'מיני מנחה.' That would support the first side, from step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of meal offering (singular)
He brings one
This implies. It introduces something learned from what the text leaves out.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"A meal offering," "a type of meal offering": he brings one,
which implies that "types of a meal offering" means two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from steps 9 and 10 in favor of step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What the opening clause of the משנה implies: 'מנחה, מין מנחה – יביא אחת.'

steps.title: The later clause implies the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: look at the later clause of the משנה. 'מנחות' or 'מין מנחות' requires two, which implies that 'מיני מנחה' requires only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the later clause: 'Meal offerings' or 'a type of meal offerings' means he brings two. So 'types of a meal offering' would mean one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading the same kind of implication from the משנה's later clause, and it points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later clause limits the 'bring two' rule to wordings where 'מנחות' itself is plural. By the same method, 'מיני מנחה,' where the word מנחה is singular, should be only one. So the two clauses of the משנה pull in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Meal offerings (plural)
A type of meal offerings

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the later clause disproves the 'two' side. It only cancels the proof. Each clause implies a different answer, so neither one decides.

phrases.english: Say the later clause:
"Meal offerings," "a type of meal offerings": he brings two,
which implies that "types of a meal offering" means one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 11 with an opposite implication from the same משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Cancels the proof from the opening clause; it does not decide the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The opening clause and the later clause of the משנה imply opposite answers, so relying on one clause's implication is not reliable.

steps.title: No proof can be drawn from this משנה
steps.stepSummary: Since the two clauses contradict each other, the גמרא concludes that the משנה teaches nothing about 'מיני מנחה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, nothing can be learned from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: this משנה cannot answer רב פפא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one clause implies 'two' and the other implies 'one,' the משנה simply did not deal with this wording. רב פפא's question stays open, as far as this משנה goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces the corrected conclusion.
Nothing can be learned from it

steps.whatToRemember: For 'מיני מנחה,' each clause of the משנה implies a different answer, so the משנה gives no proof. The question of one מנחה or two stays unresolved here.

phrases.english: Rather, from this nothing can be learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the contradiction shown in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is neutral on 'מיני מנחה'; רב פפא's question is not settled by it.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to show that 'מיני מנחה' means one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: 'מין מנחות' requires two מנחות of one type. So 'ממיני מנחה' should require only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone says 'meal offerings of a type are on me,' he brings two meal offerings of one type. That implies that 'of the types of a meal offering' means just one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof for רב פפא's question, this time from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the plural word 'מנחות' is what makes him owe two. So when the word is the singular 'מנחה,' as in 'ממיני מנחה,' he should owe only one. This supports the 'one' side of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the types of a meal offering': plural 'types,' singular 'offering'
Of one type

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'Meal offerings of a type are upon me'
he brings two meal offerings of one type,
this implies that for 'of the types of a meal offering,' he brings one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה gave no answer (step 13), the גמרא turns to a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The 'one' side of רב פפא's question
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'מין מנחות' requires two of one type, which implies 'ממיני מנחה' requires one.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא implies two offerings from two types
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the ברייתא could just as well imply that 'מיני מנחה' requires two מנחות from two different types.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the implication is this: for 'types of a meal offering,' he brings two meal offerings from two types.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by offering a different way to read what the ברייתא implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said that 'מין' (one type) leads to two offerings of one type. The contrast could be about the word 'type' and not the word 'offering': plural 'מיני' (types) would mean two offerings from two types. So the ברייתא might really support the 'two' side.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; maybe it means something else
From two types

phrases.english: Perhaps this implies that for 'types of a meal offering,'
he brings two meal offerings, from two types.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference from the ברייתא only, not the ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contrast in the ברייתא could be read as being about 'one type vs. many types,' which points to two offerings.

steps.title: The full ברייתא already covers two types, so 'מיני מנחה' must mean one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the rejection: the full ברייתא already says 'מיני מנחות' means two from two types, so 'מיני מנחה' must be different and require only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not how the ברייתא is taught. It says: 'meal offerings of a type are on me': he brings two of one type. 'Types of meal offerings are on me': he brings two from two types. That implies 'types of a meal offering' means one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 15 by quoting the whole ברייתא, which already has a separate case for two offerings from two types.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already uses 'מיני מנחות' (plural 'offerings') for two offerings from two types. If 'מיני מנחה' meant the same thing, the ברייתא's wording would be pointless. So the singular 'מנחה' must mean just one, and the proof for the 'one' side seems to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not taught that way; the text does not say that
'Types of meal offerings': plural 'types' and plural 'offerings'

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the one-letter-level difference: 'מיני מנחות' (plural offerings) requires two from two types, while 'מיני מנחה' (singular offering) is the case רב פפא asked about.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught like this:
'Meal offerings of a type are upon me'
he brings two meal offerings of one type;
'Types of meal offerings are upon me'
he brings two meal offerings from two types;
this implies that for 'types of a meal offering,' he brings one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 15 using the full wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 15 that 'מיני מנחה' means two from two types
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already gives 'מיני מנחות' that meaning, so 'מיני מנחה' must mean something else: just one.

steps.title: The ברייתא may follow רבי שמעון, who allows one מנחה with two kinds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא may follow רבי שמעון. For him, 'מיני מנחה' can mean one מנחה made of two kinds of baked dough, half loaves and half wafers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון, who said one may bring half loaves and half wafers. And what does 'types of a meal offering' mean? A meal offering that has two types in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by saying the ברייתא may follow only רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows a single מנחה to be half loaves and half wafers. For him, 'מיני מנחה' can mean 'one מנחה with two kinds inside it,' and that is why one is enough. Those who argue with him do not allow mixing, so for them the phrase may still mean two offerings, and רב פפא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
Loaves, thick baked cakes
Wafers, thin baked cakes
Half
Two types

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not settle רב פפא's question. It may follow רבי שמעון, who could explain 'מיני מנחה' as a single מנחה with two kinds of dough. That reason does not hold for the opinion that forbids mixing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic move: a proof is pushed aside by tying the source to one תנא's view, so it cannot decide the question for everyone.

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא הָא מַנִּי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא,
phrases.english: Perhaps, whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: מֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין יָבִיא,
phrases.english: who said: he may bring half loaves and half wafers,
and what does 'types of a meal offering' mean?
A meal offering that has two types in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא הָא מַנִּי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by limiting the ברייתא to רבי שמעון's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא as a ruling for all opinions
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'one' ruling may come from רבי שמעון's special view that one מנחה can contain two kinds, which the other opinion does not accept.

steps.title: For the רבנן, two types means two separate offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its rejection. For רבי שמעון, 'מיני מנחה' can be one offering of mixed loaves and wafers. But the רבנן forbid that mix, so for them it must be two מנחות of two different types.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the רבנן, who say that one may not bring half loaves and half wafers in one offering, a person who said 'מיני מנחה' brings two meal offerings of two different types.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the rejection from the previous step. It explains what 'מיני מנחה' would mean for the רבנן, who disagree with רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the ברייתא might follow רבי שמעון, where one מנחה can hold two kinds of baked items. The רבנן do not allow mixing loaves and wafers in one offering. So for them, 'two kinds' can only be met by bringing two whole מנחות of two types. This shows the ברייתא gives no firm proof for the plain view, because its meaning depends on whose opinion it follows.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not bring (the רבנן do not allow a mixed offering)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: one מנחה may be half loaves and half wafers. רבנן: no mixing, so 'two kinds' means two separate מנחות. That is why the ברייתא's proof fell apart.

phrases.english: But the Rabbis, who say:

phrases.aramaic: מֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין – לֹא יָבִיא,
phrases.english: half loaves and half wafers – he may not bring,
he brings two meal offerings of two types.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in Step 17 by showing how the רבנן would read 'מיני מנחה'.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא (Step 16) that 'מיני מנחה' requires only one offering.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could follow רבי שמעון, where one mixed offering counts as two kinds. For the רבנן, 'מיני מנחה' would mean two separate offerings, so no single reading is forced.

steps.title: Who taught the rule of bringing all five
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone who specified a מנחה but forgot which one brings all five types. It asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'I specified, but I don't know what I specified' – he brings all five. Who is the תנא who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five types of מנחה are סולת, מחבת, מרחשת, oven-baked loaves, and oven-baked wafers. The משנה assumes that bringing these five covers every possibility. The גמרא wants to know which תנא would agree that five is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: I specified (I named which kind of מנחה I was vowing)
He brings all five (types of מנחה)
Who is the תנא? (whose opinion is this)

phrases.english: "I specified, and I do not know what I specified"
– he brings all five.
Who taught this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'מיני מנחה' discussion and opens a new question on a different clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that bringing the five types of מנחה covers a forgotten specified vow.

steps.title: This rule cannot follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון. Since רבי שמעון allows an offering of half loaves and half wafers, five offerings would not cover every possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is not like רבי שמעון. If it were רבי שמעון, then since he said a person may bring half loaves and half wafers, five would not be enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question: the משנה is not the view of רבי שמעון. He explains that רבי שמעון's view would create more possibilities than five offerings can cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, an oven-baked מנחה could be all loaves, all wafers, or a mix. So the person might have vowed a mixed offering, and bringing one all-loaves and one all-wafers offering would not cover it. The משנה says five is enough, so it must follow the רבנן, who forbid the mix.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not in line with (someone's opinion)
Since (introduces the reason)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון's sentence here ends with יָבִיא ('he may bring') and not לֹא יָבִיא. That one word is the whole difference between him and the רבנן in Step 18.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is not like Rabbi Shimon,
for if it were Rabbi Shimon –
since he said
half loaves and half wafers – he may bring.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the conclusion unsaid: with mixes allowed, five offerings would not cover every possible vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה does not follow רבי שמעון. His view allows mixed loaf-and-wafer offerings, so five offerings would not be enough.

steps.title: Even counting ten items, there would be fourteen possibilities
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה shows how many possibilities there would be under רבי שמעון. Even using רבי יהודה's count of ten items per מנחה, the doubt would cover fourteen different offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if he holds like רבי יהודה, who says every מנחה comes as ten items, there is still a doubt between fourteen different offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה finishes his answer by counting the possibilities. Under רבי שמעון the forgetful person would need fourteen offerings, not five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ten items, an oven offering could be 10 loaves, 9 loaves and 1 wafer, and so on down to 10 wafers. That makes 11 options. Add סולת, מחבת and מרחשת, and the total is 14. Since the משנה says five, רבי ירמיה concludes it does not follow רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: even if
Are brought as ten (items per offering)
To be in doubt about
Fourteen

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ירמיה, the משנה's 'bring all five' only works for the רבנן, who forbid mixing loaves and wafers. Under רבי שמעון there would be at least fourteen possibilities. In the next step, אביי disagrees.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a single disagreement (may one offering be mixed?) changes the practical outcome for someone in doubt, from five offerings to fourteen.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Even if he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: Usually אִי נָמֵי means 'alternatively,' but here it means 'even if.'

phrases.english: who said all meal offerings come as ten,
phrases.notes: Ten loaves or wafers per offering. That is the smallest count, so the number of possibilities is the lowest it could be.

phrases.english: there is a doubt among fourteen meal offerings.
phrases.notes: There are 11 loaf-and-wafer splits (10-0 through 0-10), plus סולת, מחבת and מרחשת, for 14 in total.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי ירמיה's answer by counting how many offerings רבי שמעון's view would require.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ירמיה: under רבי שמעון, even with ten items per offering, there would be fourteen possible offerings. Five is not enough, so the משנה follows the רבנן. אביי disputes this in step 22.

steps.title: אביי: The משנה can follow רבי שמעון after all
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבי ירמיה. He says the משנה can follow רבי שמעון, because רבי שמעון allows a person to bring an offering and make a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי שמעון. We know that רבי שמעון holds a person can bring an offering and attach a condition to it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבי ירמיה's claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי שמעון. He says the problem of 'too many possibilities' can be solved with a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה thought five offerings could not cover all the options under רבי שמעון. אביי answers that the person can bring the five types, with plenty of loaves and wafers, and say: 'Whatever I really promised counts as my obligation, and the rest is a voluntary gift.' So the doubt is fully covered, and the משנה fits רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the case fits this opinion too)
He brings the offering and makes a condition

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי שמעון forbids the half loaves and half wafers offering. He agrees רבי שמעון allows it. He is only saying a condition solves the problem of too many possibilities.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Shimon,
for we have heard about Rabbi Shimon
that he said: one brings the offering and makes a condition.
phrases.notes: He means the condition is: if I owe this, it counts as what I owe. If I don't, it is a voluntary gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ירמיה's answer from steps 20-21 and gives a different answer to the question in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי ירמיה's claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי ירמיה left out that רבי שמעון allows bringing an offering with a condition, which covers every possibility.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא about a doubtful מצורע
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts quoting a ברייתא where רבי שמעון says the person brings his אשם and his לוג of oil on the next day. This is the source for רבי שמעון's rule of bringing with a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, on the next day he brings his אשם and his לוג of oil.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings his source showing that רבי שמעון allows bringing an offering with a condition. The ברייתא keeps going after this line, so the full proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about a person who is not sure if he is a real מצורע. A real מצורע brings an אשם and a לוג of oil when he becomes pure. רבי שמעון says this person in doubt still brings them, and as the ברייתא goes on, he will attach a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, a skin affliction that makes him impure
A guilt offering. Here it is the special one a מצורע brings when he becomes pure
A measure of oil the מצורע brings along with his offerings
On the next day

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says,
on the next day he brings his guilt offering and his log of oil
phrases.notes: 'The next day' means the day after his seven days of purification. The quote keeps going after this line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule of מייתי ומתני that אביי credited to רבי שמעון in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a person in doubt may bring an offering with a condition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a doubtful מצורע who brings his אשם and לוג of oil.
